speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; can you describe exactly what you felt, such as spinning sensations or just dizziness, and how long it has been happening?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The symptoms you described—sudden onset of spinning room sensation lasting exactly 3 minutes while lying down, with nausea and vomiting but now feeling back to baseline—are classic for BPPV. Do you have any history of recent head trauma, ear infections, or migraines? REQUEST TEST: Audiometry; REQUEST IMAGES: High-resolution CT temporal bone (only if hearing loss or neurological deficits are present to rule out stroke or vestibular schwannoma).
